thread.title: INEC and Police Tighten Security for 2027 Elections
thread.title_full: INEC and Police Tighten Security for 2027 Elections

author: GuardianNigeria
title: INEC and Police Tighten Security for 2027 Elections
text:
INEC and the Nigeria Police announce new logistics and security measures for the 2027 general elections, targeting difficult terrain and security hotspots to ensure safe, neutral polls.
INEC and the Nigeria Police Force have unveiled new logistics and security plans for the 2027 general elections, targeting difficult terrain and security hotspots to prevent electoral violence and reduce political tensions.
The measures were announced on Thursday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Savannah Centre for Diplomacy, Democracy and Development's Council of the Wise to the police leadership at the Force Headquarters.
Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Nadada, said the ongoing exercise would help determine areas requiring additional personnel and operational attention before, during and after the polls.
Police Strengthen Election Security Measures
AIG Ako Gabriel said the police are implementing measures to strengthen election security, including personnel training, threat assessment and engagement with political actors and other stakeholders.
The Force said the exercise would help identify areas needing extra personnel and operational focus throughout the electoral process.
Earlier, Chairman of the Council of the Wise and former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, urged the police to strengthen early warning systems and response mechanisms to prevent electoral violence.
Ariwoola, represented by council member Shuaibu Oba AbdulRaheem, said the police should monitor candidates' utterances during campaigns at all levels.
He called for prompt cautioning of those making inflammatory statements capable of inciting violence.
He urged the Inspector-General of Police to ensure adequate deployment of personnel to protect voters, polling centres, electoral materials and INEC officials.
The council chairman stressed that police officers deployed for election duties must remain neutral and professional throughout the electoral process.
Ariwoola said the council was concerned about violence that characterised some previous elections, recalling that the 2011 general elections were followed by killings and destruction of property, particularly in northern Nigeria.
INEC Addresses Logistics Challenges in Difficult Terrain
Meanwhile, INEC has commenced moves to address logistical challenges in difficult terrain and security-threatened areas ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission on Thursday inaugurated a logistics committee to develop strategies for the safe and timely movement of sensitive and non-sensitive election materials through road, air and maritime channels.
The commission appointed National Commissioner, Retired Rear Admiral Jamila Abubakar-Sadiq, as chairperson of the committee.
INEC Chairman, Amupitan, who inaugurated the committee in Abuja, said effective logistics was critical to the success of elections, stressing that essential materials must reach polling units at the appointed time.
He said the committee would adopt a multi-agency approach, bringing together military and paramilitary institutions, security agencies and transport organisations to improve coordination and operational efficiency.
Amupitan said the committee's responsibilities included assessing the logistical requirements for the 2027 elections, developing plans for the storage, distribution, deployment and retrieval of election materials, and auditing the readiness of warehouses, vehicles, airports, seaports and other transport facilities.
Security Assurances and Election Timelines
National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu (retd.) has assured Nigerians of safety and the neutrality of the nation's security agencies in the forthcoming 2027 general elections.
Speaking at the State House in Abuja on Thursday, Ribadu also said that the President would soon inaugurate a set of new aircraft to show Nigerians that the issue of security is on the front burner.
He explained that the meeting with the President was to brief him on the security situation within the country in view of the coming elections.
Ribadu, who was accompanied by heads of security agencies, said that Tinubu made it very clear he wanted to ensure safety and security for all Nigerians.
He assured voters that they will not be intimidated and that everyone should come out and vote for whoever they want.
He assured political parties, particularly those in the opposition, that security personnel would remain professional and politically neutral in the discharge of their duties.
He said nobody is going to intimidate them for whatever reasons, adding that we are all professionals and fully committed.
The assurance comes amid continuing concerns over insecurity in several parts of the country and the need to prevent violence and criminal activities from undermining preparations for the 2027 general elections.
The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to be held on January 16, while the governorship and House of Assembly elections will be conducted on February 6.
